title: On Slipping on the wet stone step
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：slip　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 slip 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1992 the fisherman ① slipped on the wet stone step without a word of thanks, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② slips on the wet stone step at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ slip on the wet stone step at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ slipped on the wet stone step before — a line in the logbook for July 1986 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Slipping on the wet stone step without a word of thanks, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ slip out before the others woke at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Slip out before the others woke at once and never mention it again.

By 1999 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ slips out before the others woke without a word of thanks every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ slipped on the wet stone step again when nobody else would.

⑩ To slip on the wet stone step, my mother said in 2004, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody slips on the wet stone step at once again and somebody must slip on the wet stone step without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 滑倒（一般过去式 slipped on the wet stone step：1992 年渔人头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 滑倒（一般现在 slips on the wet stone step：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 滑倒（不定式 to slip on the wet stone step：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 滑倒（过去完成时 had slipped on the wet stone step：1986 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 滑倒（动名词 slipping on the wet stone step 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 溜（slip out before the others woke：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去溜趁别人没醒溜了出去）
G. v. 溜（slip out before the others woke：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 滑倒（后段两处：新来的船工照例 slips out before the others woke，而母亲又一次 slipped on the wet stone step）

answers.why: slip 意为“滑倒”，1992 年渔人不图一句谢滑倒在湿石阶上滑了一跤，那是渔港里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 slipped。
slip 意为“滑倒”，自那以后渔人二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 slips。
slip 意为“滑倒”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯滑倒在湿石阶上滑了一跤”，此处为不定式 to slip on the wet stone step。
slip 意为“滑倒”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1999 年之前就有人滑倒过，故用过去完成时 had slipped。
slip 意为“滑倒”，渔人说“滑倒在湿石阶上滑了一跤这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 slipping on the wet stone step 作主语。
slip 意为“溜”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去溜趁别人没醒溜了出去”，should ever 之后用原形 slip out before the others woke。
slip 意为“溜”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻溜趁别人没醒溜了出去（slip out before the others woke at once），以后再也不要提起。
slip 意为“滑倒”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例溜趁别人没醒溜了出去，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 slips。
slip 意为“滑倒”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢滑倒在湿石阶上滑了一跤，用一般过去式 slipped 叙述。
slip 意为“滑倒”，结尾那句是母亲 2004 年的话：要滑倒在湿石阶上滑了一跤，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 slip 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1992 the fisherman slipped on the wet stone step without a word of thanks, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman slips on the wet stone step at once whenever the harbour asks.
Slipping on the wet stone step without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever slip out before the others woke at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour slips out before the others woke without a word of thanks every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother slipped on the wet stone step again, and the harbour remembered that half.
